effect: Arms a bomb counter: after a set number of bombs a flower power-up appears (4 bombs, 4 fire and the remote primer, kept into the next stage)

Bombs to place (table $02:4943, areas 1-4): Forest 10/20/30/15, Ocean 20/30/40/15, Wind 20/30/30/15, Cloud 15/20/30/20, Evil 20/30/10/20. GameFAQs lists the code. First Europe cart: the same ($02:492C, $02:48EC); armed 40 on Ocean 3 ($C34C = 1, $C34D = 40). The flower lasts past the stage: taken on Forest 2 (password 3905) and the stage cleared through its door, Forest 3 starts with 4 bombs and 4 fire; 1 and 1 without it.

effect: Hudson's infrared file exchange: a file menu with KISS MAIL and the KISS MONSTER2 battle game, played face to face with another Game Boy
note: Japan only (HuC-1 cart with an infrared LED). Title, Start, then the third line of the mode menu; it is there only off a Super Game Boy ($C1A2 = 0, set at boot from the SGB multiplayer check $00:3641; the menu $01:4FCB). The GB KISS kernel is in bank 0 (RST $08 system calls), the infrared driver in bank $1E (LED on with $0E to $0000, then bit 0 of $A000), the menu in bank $1F. A fresh cart registers KISS MAIL and KISS-MON2 (from bank $1D, run from RAM). In Mesen: the menu, KISS MAIL's editor, and KISS MONSTER2's name entry, point sharing and battle screen; every transfer waits for a partner (通信準備中です) and B gives 通信トラブル!, since one emulated Game Boy has no partner.

GameShark. $C2CC is cleared at every start and set only by the unused debug decoder; the two player-death checks ($02:436B, $02:4DC3) skip when it is set, and so does the clock running out. Mesen: 0 deaths in 2 x 20,000 frames of the random-input bot (40 deaths with infinite lives on). Game Genie: the ROM patch below, same bot test.

effect: Japanese menu and label graphics left in: はじめから / パスワード, かんたん / ふつう / むずかしい, the kana world names
note: The loader ($00:163C) copies 2 KB blocks from the table at $0C:6F44. Four blocks are Japanese text the release replaced with English ones, and the code still loads the Japanese number first and overwrites it on the next instruction: LD B,$19 then LD B,$43 ($01:5E10, $01:5EE9, $02:5865), $2E then $44 ($01:6B2B, $03:482F), $2F then $45 ($03:483B), and $3F for $46 at $02:4629. Changing the operand back (file $5E12, $5EEB, $6467 to $19; $6B2E, $C832 to $2E; $862A to $3F) shows them in Mesen (Game Boy Color): the New Game menu reads はじめから / パスワード and LICENSED BY NINTENDO, the world plates show kana (モリ for Forest), and LEVEL SELECT reads かんたん / ふつう / むずかしい. The menu that names the modes comes out scrambled, as the English layout points at other tiles. Block $2F's first 768 bytes (ただいまのけっか, ranking text) were not shown. Static: the first European cart has the same double loads (LD B,$19 then $43 at $01:4C1E, $01:4CE5, $02:57EE; $2E then $44 at $01:591C, $03:4815; $2F then $45 at $03:4821; $46 at $02:460C) and blocks $19, $2E and $3F byte-identical to the US ones ($2F matches Japan's); the Japanese cart shows these graphics in normal play, so it is not added.

effect: A looping tune no world plays

effect: A rising whoosh the game never plays
note: Sounds go through $00:254E ($C1C1 = function, $C1C2 = number): 212 calls with the number written in and two music tables, none giving effect 0F. Its data ($12:48DC, noise channel) is the only unrequested effect not shared with Hudson's other Game Boy games. About 0.55 s, a noise burst rising in pitch. Recorded in BizHawk with the music muted. Static: sound bank $12 (effect 0F at $12:48DC) is byte-identical on both monochrome carts, and none of the constant effect requests through their moved entry ($00:20DA / $00:1ED0) asks for 0F, as on the US cart.
